chapter: Later years and the Texas scene
title: The Alamo City Jazz Band and falling out
summary: Albert helped form the band and album with Jim Cullen but quarrelled over prejudice and the record's mix.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: What about people like the Alamo City Jazz Band or the Happy Jazz Band? Anybody out there in Texas, did you play with them ever?

I'm responsible for them organizing that band. Which one? The album? The album. The album. The album. Both of them. Both of them. Both of them. Because they came to me to make an album. And little Jim Cullen wasn't even playing. So I agreed to make the album. But the thing that happened on, as I told you before, I let those men do most of the playing. And when they brought it to Frank Triggs, a friend of mine in Columbia, they said, well, I don't have enough of Don Alvin on. And no voice. And now we're in that solo. So from that then, we had a falling out of personal things. I thought they were real prejudice, which was proven to me on one of my engagements with them on Mike Wallace's program. And so I just pulled away.
And you didn't play with Alamo City? No. No. No.

And I only played maybe once or twice with Jim because, like I said, the reception that I got from them wasn't what I thought it should be. And it caused a close relationship with people. It was one of these distant things. And I just stayed as close as I could. But I have a, I will say this, that Jim Cullen was a nice fella, a likable fella. And to me, he wasn't the greatest clarinetist in the world. But he did have a soulful feeling in his playing. And it was pleasing. He could enjoy it. And I went to his grave site.
